transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-06-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-record-48271
Attendees: Sofia M. (Redwood AE), Daniel C. (Redwood SE), Rajiv P. (Helix Head of Partnerships), Maya T. (Helix Cloud SA), Ethan L. (Helix CTO)

Summary (auto):
- Intro between Helix Integrations (partner/reseller) and Redwood Inference; discuss go-to-market and technical fit for joint offerings.
- Primary topics: partner program, deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), compliance (SOC2/KMS), benchmarking plan and POC scope.
- Agreed next steps: share docs, benchmark template, and schedule POC kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Today Daniel from our SE team will run through a quick tech overview and then we'll talk go-to-market.
[00:18] Rajiv Patel: Hi all, Rajiv here. We're excited to chat — Helix does cloud orchestration and channel partnerships, we see lots of customers asking for an inference runtime option.
[00:28] Daniel Cho: Hey, yeah, hi. Quick one — I'll try to keep it light on slides. We'll cover Redwood product modes, perf tradeoffs, and integration points with partners like Helix.
[00:40] Maya Thompson: Good — we have some infra folks listening in the back, might drop questions.
[00:46] Ethan Li: Welcome. From our side the key is predictable throughput and the ability to offer managed on-prem for regulated customers.
[00:54] Sofia Martinez: Perfect, that's good context. Rajiv, can you give a quick overview of typical Helix customers and where you see the fit?
[01:10] Rajiv Patel: Sure — most of our customers are mid-enterprise SaaS and some regulated healthcare fintechs; they care about data residency and audit logs. They also expect channel pricing and co-selling motion.
[01:26] Daniel Cho: Got it. On the Redwood side — we have three primary serving modes: hosted API (fastest to onboard), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput and isolation), and Private (VPC / on-prem with a private control plane).
[01:44] Rajiv Patel: Private sounds interesting. When you say "private control plane" — how much of that is SaaS call-outs vs customer-managed?
[01:54] Daniel Cho: Good question. For Private we offer a control plane that can be deployed into the customer's VPC, optionally with an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. You can run control plane ops via your own KMS/HSM and we support SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[02:12] Maya Thompson: Okay, SAML and KMS are must-haves — our customers need KMS integration and also good audit trails. Do you have SOC 2?
[02:20] Sofia Martinez: Yes — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we publish audit logs; we also have ISO work in progress. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[02:30] Ethan Li: Are those documents public or under an NDA?
[02:34] Sofia Martinez: We can share a redacted pack pre-NDA; full artifacts usually require a signed AFA or NDA.
[02:42] Rajiv Patel: Makes sense. On pricing — our partners want predictable reseller margins. Do you have partner tiers?
[02:50] Sofia Martinez: We do — basic partner, reseller, and strategic. Reseller tiers include negotiated discounts and co-sell credits; I'll send details.
[02:58] Daniel Cho: To add — on the tech side, one key tradeoff we see is latency vs cost. Hosted is easiest but can be more variable on latency; Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools for SLOs, and Private is best for compliance but requires more ops.
[03:16] Maya Thompson: For our regulated customers, they lean toward private or dedicated. They also ask about model compatibility — can you run custom models or only curated ones?
[03:26] Daniel Cho: We support curated open models and also customer-provided models; for Private we can onboard their weights. There are compatibility checks — model architecture, quantization profile, and kernel choices.
[03:36] Rajiv Patel: You mentioned quantization — do you support int8 or other low-precision options for cost savings?
[03:42] Daniel Cho: Yes — our runtime supports quantization-friendly paths, often int8 and bfloat16 depending on hardware. For certain architectures we recommend specific quant formats.
[03:50] Ethan Li: Speaking of hardware, what GPU vendors do you certify? We routinely sell infra from multiple vendors.
[03:58] Daniel Cho: We optimize for NVIDIA and AMD and have tuning for various clouds; we also run benchmarks on common instance types. We have a kernel selection layer that picks the best kernels per hardware.
[04:10] Rajiv Patel: We've seen mention of Triton and Bedrock — any dependence on those?
[04:15] Daniel Cho: No dependence. We can run alongside Triton or on in-house runtimes but are not built on Bedrock — that's a competitor in some deployments.
[04:23] Maya Thompson: For integration — can Helix bundle Redwood as a managed add-on in the console? API keys, per-tenant metering?
[04:31] Sofia Martinez: Yes — we have API/SDKs, token-based auth, and per-route/model dashboards in the Console. We can provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns so Helix can pass billing info back to their customers.
[04:44] Rajiv Patel: Great. On meterings — do you provide usage webhooks or a reporting API for downstream billing?
[04:50] Daniel Cho: We have reporting APIs and can push aggregated usage; webhooks are on our roadmap but we can work with the partner team to deliver a receipts feed.
[05:00] Maya Thompson: About benchmarks — could we run a small standardized benchmark to show cost/latency for a few models for our sales motion?
[05:06] Daniel Cho: Absolutely. We usually run a 3-model benchmark (small, med, large) across typical sequence lengths and provide a spreadsheet. I'll share a template.
[05:14] Rajiv Patel: What about cold start and batching behavior? Many of our customers are real-time chat apps.
[05:20] Daniel Cho: Our runtime has continuous batching and KV cache management; cold start depends on model size and whether KV cache is warm. For chat SLOs we recommend Dedicated for consistent latency, plus prefix caching.
[05:32] Ethan Li: For POC scope — can we do a private POC where we supply infra and Redwood runs the control plane in our VPC?
[05:40] Daniel Cho: Yes. Typical POC: 2-week technical validation, we onboard a model (or run our reference models), run load tests, and validate metrics and security controls. For private POC we do an operator-run with our SE and your infra engineers.
[05:52] Sofia Martinez: Rajiv, is Helix looking to resell or co-sell, or both?
[05:58] Rajiv Patel: Both. Ideally resell for smaller deals, co-sell on strategic accounts. We'll need partner pricing and a simple onboarding flow for our sales team.
[06:08] Sofia Martinez: We can enable a reseller onboarding kit — include docs, playbooks, and a partner dev sandbox.
[06:14] Maya Thompson: Sandbox access — can we get a short-lived API token and a demo tenant to run integration tests?
[06:20] Daniel Cho: Yes — we can provision trial tokens for partner sandbox. They usually expire after 30 days unless extended.
[06:27] Rajiv Patel: Security question — is log data ever sent to Redwood in Private mode? Our customers will want assurance that logs are local.
[06:34] Daniel Cho: In Private with customer-managed control plane, logs stay in the customer's environment by default. We can forward metrics optionally.
[06:40] Ethan Li: Great. Any specifics on network egress/costs when using hosted vs private?
[06:45] Sofia Martinez: We can provide estimates; private deployments tend to have customer-managed egress so it's under their cloud bill. Hosted has our egress costs included. We'll send a short runbook.
[06:56] Maya Thompson: For compliance, do you have data residency controls per tenant?
[07:02] Daniel Cho: Yes — routing policies can pin requests to regions and model variants. We also support per-tenant data retention policies and audit logs.
[07:10] Rajiv Patel: Switching gears — what does enablement look like for partners? How long to get an SE up to speed to run demos?
[07:18] Sofia Martinez: We provide partner onboarding sessions, an SE enablement program (2-3 sessions) and a partner portal with quickstarts and example stacks. SE ramp typically 1-2 weeks to be comfortable with common demos.
[07:30] Daniel Cho: We also provide sample Helm charts and deployment manifests for Private and Dedicated so integration is plug-and-play for common clouds.
[07:38] Maya Thompson: Helm charts — perfect. Will those include quantization profiles and runtime knobs?
[07:44] Daniel Cho: Yes, the charts include default config maps with batching, kernel selection, quantization profile hints. They're opinionated but editable.
[07:52] Rajiv Patel: A few customers ask for on-prem air-gapped installs — how heavy is the operator involvement?
[07:58] Daniel Cho: We have an operator-run path and a self-hosted path. For air-gapped installs, our team typically does the initial ops and hands over documentation; timeline depends on environment but 2-4 weeks is typical for a minimal install.
[08:12] Ethan Li: For the POC, we want to validate throughput: 200 concurrent chat users, 4-turn convo, 512 token box. Is that feasible?
[08:20] Daniel Cho: Should be feasible on Dedicated or Private with appropriate GPU sizing. We'll map model choice to hardware; the benchmark template will help calculate QPS and token cost.
[08:30] Maya Thompson: About costs — can you share unit economics like tokens/sec and $/1M tokens for common configs?
[08:36] Sofia Martinez: We'll include typical unit economics in the partner packet — approximate $/1M tokens for hosted, and reference allocation for Dedicated. Exact reseller pricing is negotiable.
[08:46] Rajiv Patel: Any roadblocks you see for Helix to onboard as a partner quickly?
[08:52] Sofia Martinez: Not many; main items are legal (partner MSA), security review, and a short enablement. We can fast-track the MSA for strategic partners.
[09:02] Rajiv Patel: Legal — do you have a partner MSA template we can share with our legal?
[09:06] Sofia Martinez: Yes — I'll attach the partner MSA and a redline guide.
[09:12] Maya Thompson: On the technical side, we'll want a checklist of the ports/protocols and minimum HW.
[09:18] Daniel Cho: I'll add an infrastructure checklist to the benchmark packet — ports, instance types, and recommended GPU SKUs.
[09:26] Rajiv Patel: For co-selling, is there a partner portal for leads and deal registration?
[09:30] Sofia Martinez: We do deal registration in the partner portal; we'll grant Helix a partner account and show the process.
[09:36] Ethan Li: Sounds good. For the POC, can we include a short security demo showing SSO and audit log export?
[09:42] Daniel Cho: Yes — typical POC scope includes SSO, audit log verification, and sample load tests.
[09:48] Rajiv Patel: Timing — we'd like to kickoff POC mid-June.
[09:52] Sofia Martinez: We'll aim to have the documents and scheduling options out by next week so you can pick dates.
[09:58] Maya Thompson: Perfect. A few quick clarifications — does Redwood support tenant-level model pinning?
[10:04] Daniel Cho: Yes — per-tenant model pinning and rollout policies, canary deploys and automatic fallback to smaller model variants if a model fails.
[10:12] Rajiv Patel: That fallback is handy. We may want to white label some of the telemetry — is that possible?
[10:18] Sofia Martinez: We can surface telemetry via API; white labeling dashboards is possible for Dedicated/Private with some customization.
[10:26] Maya Thompson: If we do a reseller motion, what does billing look like? Do you invoice Helix or the end-customer?
[10:34] Sofia Martinez: For reselling, Redwood invoices the partner (Helix) and the partner handles billing to end-customers. For co-sell, we can invoice the end customer and coordinate via partner credits.
[10:44] Rajiv Patel: Good. Any known limitations with model sizes or sequence lengths?
[10:50] Daniel Cho: Giant models with very long sequences increase memory and may require multi-GPU sharding; we support that but it changes ops complexity. We can recommend quantized variants for giant models.
[11:02] Ethan Li: Ok — last question from me: what's the escalation path if the POC hits blocking perf issues?
[11:08] Daniel Cho: SE (me) is primary escalation, then platform eng for kernel tuning. We also have a priority channel for partner POCs.
[11:16] Rajiv Patel: Thanks everyone. Let's recap next steps.
[11:20] Sofia Martinez: Recap: I'll send partner program docs, MSA template, and security pack; Daniel will send benchmark spreadsheet and infra checklist; Maya will share workload traces; Helix to confirm POC stakeholders and dates.
[11:36] Rajiv Patel: Sounds great. We'll aim for mid-June POC kickoff.
[11:40] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all — we'll follow up by email with links. Attaching a few quick links here: Partner deck (internal): https://redwood.example/partners/helix-deck , Benchmark template: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/partner-template.xlsx
[11:58] Maya Thompson: Thanks, bye.
[12:01] Ethan Li: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
